frame: MINIMAL CHANGE — ship, don't redesign. I take the ledger's rank-1 reframe seriously but not uncritically: the two PCs' complaint is agency, not damage, and the cheapest repairs are re-parenting and re-typing existing talents, not writing new ones. Everything below is either (a) a one-token/one-line correction of something that is already wrong, or (b) a change to ONE talent that sits at a chokepoint five other talents hang off. Twelve talents are touched across proposals 1-5 (the "ship this week" set); proposals 6-8 add six more if the designer wants them. Two structural findings — heroic flat scaling (ledger #3) and the deity zero-Special count (#8) — I deliberately leave alone and say why. Session one has not happened, so every one of these is free of continuity cost; the only real costs are pack rebuilds (Ben-only) and re-running the iron-rule-7 graph gate. Every proposal names its surface (authored JSON + pack rebuild, structure JSON + pack rebuild, engine-only, or docs-only) because that determines who can land it and whether Ben has to touch Foundry.

proposals.title: The errata pass — eight one-line corrections of things that are already wrong
proposals.change: Eight independent edits, none of which is a design decision. (1) data/leyline.json:840 Counterspell cost `"2 Focus; 1 Investiure"` -> `"2 Focus; 1 Investiture"`. (2) leyline/White Interposing Shield: `reduce that damage by half [Die]` -> `half [Tier][Die]`, matching its two siblings Devoted Conduit and Shield Wall, in both data/leyline.json prose and data/authored/leyline-white.json if the mitigation is formula-backed. (3) data/domain.json deity/Death Raise Dead: `connections` is ["Necrotic Cascade","Risen Servant"] while the card reads "Necrotic Cascade or Speak with the Fallen" — change `connections` to ["Necrotic Cascade","Speak with the Fallen"] so the managed prerequisite matches the printed one. (4) data/domain.json deity/Death Necrotic Cascade: `connections` ["Consuming Decay","Death Ward"] vs card "Consuming Decay" — drop "Death Ward" from connections (or add it to the card; pick one, but the card is the cheaper edit to keep and the connection is the silent one). (5) deity/Power Kneel and Absolute Authority: strike the word "Frightened" from both clause lists (nothing in the 365 produces it) — leave Compelled and Weakened, which both have live suppliers. (6) deity/Chaos Unravel Everything: add "Once per scene." to match the other nine deity capstones. (7) leyline/White Shared Burden: `rankGate` reads "Strength 3+; White 2+"; Strength is an attribute, not a skill, so the rank-cap ladder does not apply — either re-express as an attribute threshold in the tooling so it re-dates off L6, or lower it to Strength 2+ and be done. (8) leyline/White Mending Aura source prose in data/leyline.json owes the authored text's cost line ("an Opportunity and 1 Investiture"); and DESIGN-GUIDE-CLAIMS.md's Black entry says the Draw Mana rider isolates at 10 ft where all three shipped talents (Black Attunement Key, Sapping Hex, Chaos's Isolated definition) use 5 ft — correct the guide, not the talents.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #5 (Frightened), #9 (Death connections, the ungated iron-rule-7 case), #15 (Interposing Shield), #16 (Chaos capstone), #18 (Counterspell typo), #19 (guide 10ft), #20 (Shared Burden + Mending Aura prose).
proposals.cost: Nothing gets weaker except deity/Chaos's capstone, which loses the ability to be cast twice in one scene — the nine-of-ten conformance case, so this is bringing it into line, not nerfing it. Retest: run `node scripts/validate.js` and `node scripts/gates.js` after the two `connections` edits (the DAG/reachability check must re-pass; Raise Dead's parent set changes). Interposing Shield's mitigation roughly doubles at Tier 2 (from ~2.0 to ~4.5) — worth one bench row. Every Blue Investiture census ever computed changes by one talent (15 -> 16) once the Counterspell typo is fixed; that is a correction, not a regression.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on all eight. These are contradictions internal to the data or between the data and its own cards; none rests on a judgment call. What would change my mind: on (3)/(4) only — if the designer says the `connections` array is the intended prerequisite and the card is the stale side, then fix the card instead. Either direction closes it; leaving them divergent is the only wrong answer.
proposals.surface: Data edit (data/leyline.json, data/domain.json, data/authored/*) + pack rebuild and Sync for the card-text items; docs-only for the DESIGN-GUIDE-CLAIMS.md radius line. Items 3, 4 and 7 are structure-file edits that also want a validate.js re-run.

proposals.title: Settle leyline/Red's Momentum's Edge with a two-minute live check, then a one-token fix
proposals.change: Before any balance conclusion about Red is acted on, evaluate `@movement.walk.rate` against a live actor in Foundry (a bench row: open a PC with a walk rate, resolve the rider, read what the damage card prints). Three outcomes, three one-token fixes. (a) It resolves to nothing (DerivedValueField object, no numeric coercion) — the talent silently does zero; change `bonusFormula` to whatever the intended term is. (b) It resolves to a movement rate in feet, ~+25-30 flat impact on a free depth-2 Passive against 1-4 for every other rider in the game — cap it, e.g. `floor(@movement.walk.rate / 10)` or replace with `@attr.spd.mod`, and reword the card so "your Speed" is unambiguous. (c) It resolves to the Speed skill modifier, ~+2 to +5 — the card is already right and only the ambiguity needs fixing (write "your Speed modifier" on the card). Do not redesign the talent; change one token and one clause.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #6. Also unblocks the whole damage-distribution answer to designer question 1 — this is the one place in the review where a single measurement decides whether leyline/Red is the best damage tree at levels 1-5 or a mid-table one, and every Red-vs-Black-vs-Knowledge comparison in the review is denominated against it.
proposals.cost: Nothing, if you check first. If you skip the check and guess: in world (b) you have shipped the largest damage rider in the game on a free Passive; in world (a) a level-3 talent does nothing and a player will never diagnose it. Retest: one bench row plus a `tests/` regression case pinning whatever the formula ends up being (iron rule 4 requires it if the fix lands in a helper).
proposals.confidence: HIGH that it needs settling; DELIBERATELY UNCOMMITTED on which world we are in — that is the honest position and the defence advocate's "probably a one-token overlay typo" and intent-drift's "live balance bug worth +20-30" are both guesses. What would change my mind: the bench read. Nothing else can settle it, and no amount of talent-text reading will.
proposals.surface: Bench check first (🤖, agent-drivable per bench-run); then a data edit in data/authored/leyline-red.json (+ card prose in data/leyline.json) and a pack rebuild. Worlds (a) and (c) are one token; world (b) is one token plus one clause.

proposals.title: leyline/Blue: re-parent Read Intent to depth 1 so the whole Calculation branch turns on at level 2 instead of level 6
proposals.change: In data/leyline.json, change Read Intent's `connections` from ["Probable Outcome"] to ["Forewarned"] (or to the Key), moving it from depth 3 / earliest L4 to depth 1 / earliest L2, and add Read Intent to Pattern Recognition's `connections` group as an OR alternative alongside Calculated Patience. Keep its text, its 1-Action cost and its 1-Investiture price exactly as they are. Optionally re-parent Probable Outcome to keep the Foresight column contiguous. This is a graph edit, not a text edit.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #1 for Blue (the acute half — Blue is the tree with 0 damage, 0 healing, 0 mitigation, 0 resource generation and three teeth all gated to L6). It is the chokepoint fix the remit asks for: Read Intent is already "1 Action, 1 Investiture, test Blue vs. Cognitive defense" — Blue's only self-initiated, repeatable, on-turn attack on a defence — and it currently sits four levels behind the three talents that require exactly that event. Pattern Recognition (depth 1, L2) needs "you succeed on a Cognitive test against a character"; Subtle Suggestion and Baleful need an influence attempt; Blue supplies the trigger for none of them before L4. Re-parenting one node gives a level-2 Blue mage a loop — Action: Read Intent (know their next move AND satisfy Pattern Recognition's trigger); Special: Pattern Recognition (their next test has disadvantage) — for 2 Investiture and 1 Action, repeatable, at level 2. That is the missing agency, and it contains no damage.
proposals.cost: Blue's Foresight column gets slightly flatter and Blue becomes noticeably stronger at L2-L5, which is the intent. Probable Outcome loses a dependent and may want re-parenting so it is not orphaned. MUST re-run `node scripts/validate.js` and `tests/pipeline.test.js`: this touches `connections`, which are managed prerequisites (iron rule 7), and the DAG plus reachability sweep has to re-pass — that is the whole gate. Also check the third, ungated case the iron rule warns about: after the edit, Read Intent's card prose and its `connections` must name the same parent. Bench: confirm Pattern Recognition actually fires off a Read Intent success (it is a `skill_test` activation against Cognitive defense, so it should, but that is an assumption about the engine's success event and it should be a 🤖 row, not an assertion).
proposals.confidence: HIGH that this is the right shape and the cheapest available Blue fix. MEDIUM that it is sufficient on its own — it fixes levels 2-5 and does nothing about Blue's five-talent disadvantage block folding into one binary scalar. What would change my mind: if the bench shows Pattern Recognition's trigger does not fire on a Read Intent success, the chokepoint is an engine wiring problem instead and this proposal becomes a wiring fix at the same node.
proposals.surface: Data edit — data/leyline.json structure (connections/prereq only), pack rebuild + ⟳ Sync. No authored-overlay change, no engine change, no new text.

proposals.title: leyline/White: re-type three talents so the tree stops spending its whole identity on one Reaction slot
proposals.change: Three edits, all cost/action-type, none touching effect text. (a) Devoted Conduit and Shield Wall are free permanent Passives that mitigate ~4.5 at Tier 2; Interposing Shield is a costed Reaction that mitigates less. After the errata fix in proposal 1 they are equal in size, which makes the Reaction pointless. Re-type Interposing Shield from `Reaction` to `Special` and keep the 10 ft move — it then rides an action White is already taking rather than competing with Retributive Guard and Shared Burden for the same trigger and the same one-per-round slot. (b) Shared Burden: drop 2 Investiture -> 1 Investiture and (with proposal 1 item 7) un-gate it from the bogus L6 date. It is the tree's bottom-ranked talent and the fix is a price, not a redesign. (c) Ordered Advance is White's only 2-Action talent and the review's worst-ranked White card: re-type it from `2 Actions` to `1 Action`. That takes White's Action-costing count from 2/25 to 2/25 by count but makes the one deep Action play affordable in the same turn as Draw Mana, which is the actual complaint. Explicitly DO NOT add a damage talent to White — see the argument field.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #1 for White (7 Reactions competing for 1 slot, of which 3 fire on the identical event "an ally near you takes damage"), plus the bottom of White's weak-talent list (Shared Burden, Ordered Advance both named). Also partially resolves the redundancy the ledger's rank-1 evidence names: after (a), the Reaction slot holds Retributive Guard (damage), Voice of Authority (disadvantage), Pillar of Order (Complication), Shared Burden (redirection) and Counterpoint (influence) — five genuinely distinct trigger classes and one interposition moved off the slot entirely.
proposals.cost: White gets meaningfully stronger defensively at levels 2-4, which is the point but it should be watched: after proposal 1 item 2 plus (a), a White mage with Guardian Stance + Interposing Shield + Devoted Conduit is mitigating on more events per round than before. Shield Wall (free, permanent, multi-target) is already the tree's best talent and none of this touches it. Retest: bench a round where an adjacent ally is hit and confirm exactly one mitigation fires per source, not three stacked — that is a real risk and it is the one thing here I would not ship unbenched. Interposing Shield as a Special needs a defined trigger to ride ("when you Draw Mana" is the tree's existing convention, per Beacon of Stability) — if that reads badly, leave it a Reaction and do only (b) and (c).
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH on (b) and (c); MEDIUM on (a). The defence advocate's objection to the White agency finding is the strongest one in the review — White is the only colour whose refuel Action is itself an effect (the Key heals every ally for Tier, Beacon of Stability rides the same Draw Mana), so White genuinely has no dead refuel round, and Revision Principle 1 says "Specials first". That objection defeats "give White more Actions"; it does not defeat "stop three Reactions fighting over one slot". What would change my mind: if the White player at the table reports that the turn feels fine and the complaint was purely "I never damage anything", then (a) is unnecessary and this drops to proposal 8 territory.
proposals.surface: Data edit — data/leyline.json (action type + cost fields) and data/authored/leyline-white.json (activation/consumes), pack rebuild + ⟳ Sync. (a) may need an engine check that the Special's trigger is one the engine already fires.

proposals.title: Two AoE repairs at the two chokepoints — Black's inverted area attack and Warrior's worthless second Strike
proposals.change: (a) leyline/Black Spoils of Isolation currently reads "Each Weakened character within Attunement Range takes vital damage equal to your tier", and Black's only two Weakened sources (the Attunement Key and Sapping Hex) both require the target to have NO ally within 5 ft. So Black's one area attack scales with how spread out the enemies are and does nothing against a clump — the exact inverse of what area damage is for. Minimal repair: change the target clause from "Each Weakened character" to "Each enemy within Attunement Range that is Weakened OR adjacent to another enemy", or simply "Each enemy within [Size] of a point in Attunement Range", and leave the damage at tier. Do not touch Sapping Hex or the Key. (b) heroic/Warrior Swift Strikes is "1 Action + 1 focus to make a second Strike with the same weapon" — per the primer, a talent that reproduces a standard action is worth roughly zero, and it is the tree's bottom-ranked card. Re-type it into a cleave: same Action, same 1 focus, the Strike hits a second enemy within your reach (or grazes it — Warrior already owns 7 of the 10 graze talents, so graze is the on-identity version). That gives the heroic atlas its first repeatable multi-enemy play before level 6, in the path most likely to hold the party's frontliner, by repairing a talent that is already dead weight.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #2, partially and deliberately. It does not fix 14 trees; it fixes the two places where the fix is a repair rather than a new capability. After (b) the heroic atlas goes from one in-scope multi-enemy talent (Meteoric Leap, depth 3, Athletics 3+, L6, unarmed) to two, one of which is depth 2 / L3 and rides an ordinary weapon. After (a) Black's AoE stops being anti-functional.
proposals.cost: (b) makes heroic/Warrior stronger, and Warrior is already the heroic atlas's damage-and-durability chassis with 13/25 Action-costing talents — this widens Warrior's lead over Agent/Envoy/Leader/Scholar, which is a real cost and the reason it is not ranked higher. Consider pricing the second target at 2 focus. (a) makes Black's 2-Action, 1-Investiture area play actually usable, which raises Black's ceiling in group fights; Black is already the tree with the game's only 2x-tier damage formula (Withering Ray) so this is not a tree that needs help — but an inverted talent is a bug regardless of whether the tree needs help. Retest: both are 🤖 bench rows (multi-target selection is exactly where the engine's targeting handlers get exercised).
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM. The census behind ledger #2 is solid and entirely inside the fence, but what the right target-count BUDGET is cannot be settled without adversary statblocks, which are out of scope. If the GM's normal encounter is one or two enemies, 14 trees at zero AoE is a non-problem and this proposal is unnecessary. What would settle it: the adversary pack's minion counts — one query, outside this fence, and it should be asked before (b) is implemented.
proposals.surface: Data edit — data/leyline.json + data/authored/leyline-black.json for (a); data/cosmere.json + data/authored/heroic-warrior.json for (b). Pack rebuild + ⟳ Sync. (b) may need an engine multi-target handler if none of the existing primitives covers "a Strike that also hits a second enemy in reach" — grep ENGINE_INDEX.md before assuming it is data-only.

proposals.title: deity/Sovereignty: fix the promise and print the colour, and only then consider the capstone radius
proposals.change: Three edits in ascending order of commitment. (a) DOCS ONLY, do this regardless: rewrite the `Signature resource: Decree — a declared law projected within a radius` line in INTENT-deity-Sovereignty.md and its twin in the deity guide so it promises what the tree ships — a single-target arbiter that walks one enemy's damage die down and one ally's up. A player reads the path description before they roll a die; promising a radius the tree cannot make is the most-felt defect in the tree. (b) DATA, cheap and high value: every Sovereignty card prints `[Tier][Die]` with no colour, and exactly one talent (Sovereign's Favor, handler `SovFavorThp00000`, formula `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2)`) is sized by White — so a player deciding between a third rank of Black and a third of White is choosing blind. Print the colour on the card: `[Tier][Die on White]`. This is the entire real content of the "Sovereignty's White 3+ is a toll booth" finding, which is otherwise refuted. (c) OPTIONAL, one talent, only if the designer wants the Decree promise KEPT rather than retracted: give the capstone `Sovereignty` a radius — it already targets one ally and one enemy for the scene at 3 Actions / 3 Investiture / once per scene, so change it to apply the +2 step to allies and the -2 step to enemies within [Size] of a point. A capstone is where a radius belongs, and it delivers the entire promised Decree gesture in one talent with no new mechanic.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #4, in the order that costs least. (a) closes the DOCUMENTATION half at zero mechanical risk. (b) closes the toll-booth complaint, which the completeness critic settled: Fate/White is the atlas's ONLY pure toll booth (zero references of any kind, `grep -c white deity-fate.json` returns 0), and Sovereignty/White is a near-dead gate whose one reference is invisible on the card. (c) closes the DESIGN half if the designer wants it closed.
proposals.cost: (a) and (b) cost nothing and break nothing. (c) is a real power increase on a capstone and it should be priced against the deity guide's own capstone rule; it also does not fix the tree's deeper problem, which is that a single die step is +1.0 average per die and is worth exactly zero against the four flat-damage riders in the corpus (Momentum of Victory, Cheap Shot, Pack Share, Vital Diagnosis). Do NOT attempt to fix that under a minimal-change framing — it is a tree rewrite. Retest: (c) is a bench row; (b) is a card-text rebuild.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on (a) and (b). MEDIUM on (c) — the defence advocate's objection to the Sovereignty finding survives on structure (Sovereign's Favor's [Tier][Die] temp HP is unmediated by the die ladder, Expose is a free L2 uncapped Investiture producer, Edict of the Fallen is a scene-long -2 steps plus party temp HP for 2 Actions at L3), so the tree is not empty and does not need rescuing. What would change my mind on (c): if the designer's answer to "was Decree a promise or a sketch" is "a sketch", do (a) and stop.
proposals.surface: (a) docs-only (dossier INTENT file + .claude/skills/deity-revision-guide). (b) data edit, data/domain.json card prose + pack rebuild. (c) data edit, data/domain.json + data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json + pack rebuild.

proposals.title: Unify the two temporary-HP writers in the engine and pick one behaviour
proposals.change: module-src/scripts/engine/28-temporary-hp.js line 6 says "the pool does not stack, a larger grant replaces a smaller one" and line 13 says "only ONE source of Temp HP at a time (a new grant OVERWRITES the old, even if smaller)" — the code implements the second (`edhaWriteTempHp` sets unconditionally; `edhaSetTempHp` is documented as overwriting any existing source). module-src/scripts/engine/51-green-restoration.js:93 `edhaGrantTempHpCross` implements the opposite (`wins = inc > (held?.value ?? 0)`, keep the higher, a tie is not a win). A third position is asserted in data: deity/Sovereignty's Sovereign's Favor card says "This talent's temporary HP does not stack", implying other temp HP does. Fix: make ONE function the single writer, delete the other path, correct the self-contradicting header, and ship a pinned regression case in tests/ (iron rule 4 requires it — this is a pure engine helper). My recommended default is keep-the-higher, because the overwriting behaviour produces the outcome a player experiences as a bug: an ally helps you and your shield gets smaller.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #7. Also un-invalidates every temp-HP-summed-over-rounds figure in the review (Order's Bear Witness, Sovereignty's swing arithmetic), which until unified should not be used as arithmetic in any tree comparison.
proposals.cost: 14 talents across 9 trees produce temporary HP (Order 3; Power, Life, Sovereignty 2 each; plus singles) and all of them change behaviour on whichever routes currently use the losing writer. Keep-the-higher makes multi-source temp HP slightly better than it is today, which is a small buff spread across nine trees. Retest: one regression test in tests/ plus one bench row driving two grants at the same target in both orders (small-then-large and large-then-small) — that is the case the two implementations disagree on.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that it must be unified. MEDIUM on which way — that is genuinely the designer's call, and the scope caveat matters: this is an engine question, not a 365-talent question, and it should be filed as an EDHA_RULINGS.md entry rather than decided in a talent review.
proposals.surface: Engine change — edit module-src/scripts/engine/28-temporary-hp.js and 51-green-restoration.js, run `node scripts/engine-assemble.js`, commit BOTH the sources and the assembled register-skills.js. NO pack rebuild needed (iron rule 1: engine-only, F5 on Ben's machine). Plus a tests/ regression case.

proposals.title: Two Tier-1 deity repairs: the talent that is literally uncastable, and the one dominated by its own parent
proposals.change: Do NOT change the `up to your tier` cap (it appears in six deity trees and eight talents; changing it is a rebalance, not a minimal edit, and the defence advocate is right that the cap is what makes level 6 a step change). Repair only the two talents the cap actually breaks. (a) deity/Civilization Trade Routes, depth 1 / L2, reads "choose two of your active Foundations" against a Foundation cap of `tier` = 1 through level 5 — it is UNCASTABLE for its first four levels of availability. Minimal fix: reword to link a Foundation to a point you designate, or exempt Foundations from the tier cap by making Lay Foundation's cap `1 + tier`. Note the related asymmetry worth one look: Civilization's Forge Construct reads "You may sustain ONE active Construct", a flat 1 that never scales with tier, uniquely among the ten sustain clauses — that is either the deliberate price of a six-talent upgrade ladder or an oversight, and it is one grep to ask. (b) deity/Chaos Spreading Omen, depth 1 / L2, places an Omen on the target "and one additional enemy... subject to your Omen cap" — with a cap of 1 it is strictly dominated by its own parent Entropy Strike through level 5. Minimal fix: exempt Spreading Omen's second Omen from the cap, or give Chaos's cap a floor of 2.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #12, in the narrowest form that removes the actual defects (one uncastable talent, one dominated talent) without touching the six-tree cap or the ~eight downstream talents that are merely weaker at Tier 1.
proposals.cost: Small power increase to two deity trees at levels 2-5, both in the direction of making a purchased talent function. If instead you raise the caps generally, you flatten the L6 step change across six trees, which the designer may want and which is not a minimal edit. Retest: bench Trade Routes at Tier 1 to confirm it resolves; validate.js for any prerequisite change.
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH on (a) — a talent that cannot be cast at the level it becomes available is unambiguously broken. MEDIUM on (b) — "dominated by its parent" is a judgment, and the deity guide wants the signature resource to be the tree's spine, so a tight Tier-1 cap may be exactly the intent. What would change my mind: if the designer says Tier 1 is meant to be one token and the tree only blooms at L6, then (b) is intended and only (a) is a bug.
proposals.surface: Data edit — data/domain.json card prose + data/authored/deity-civilization.json and deity-chaos.json, pack rebuild + ⟳ Sync.

singleFirstChange: Re-parent leyline/Blue's Read Intent from depth 3 to depth 1 (change its `connections` from ["Probable Outcome"] to ["Forewarned"]) and add it as an OR alternative in Pattern Recognition's `connections` group. One field in data/leyline.json, no new text, no new mechanic, no engine work, and no damage. It is the single change because Blue is the acute case of the two PCs that triggered this review — it is the only tree in the game with zero damage AND zero healing AND zero mitigation AND zero resource generation, and all three of its teeth (Counterspell, Ghostly Walls -> Absolute Stillness, Anticipate) are behind Blue 3+ at level 6 — and because Read Intent is Blue's ONLY self-initiated, repeatable, on-turn test against an enemy defence, currently sitting four levels behind the three talents (Pattern Recognition, Subtle Suggestion, Baleful) that require exactly that event to fire. Moving one node gives a level-2 Blue mage a real loop for 1 Action and 2 Investiture — attack their Cognitive defence, learn their next action, and impose disadvantage on their next test — where today that player has Phantom Double (2 Actions, 2 Investiture) and waits for level 6. It is the definition of the remit's "one talent at a chokepoint over five leaves". It must be landed with a `node scripts/validate.js` + `tests/pipeline.test.js` re-run, because `connections` are managed prerequisites and iron rule 7's DAG and reachability gates have to re-pass.
argumentOnBlueWhiteDamage:
NEITHER TREE SHOULD GET A DAMAGE TALENT. I hold this against the designer's explicit permission to add one, and here is the argument rather than the assertion.

First, the premise is half wrong on the facts. White is not a no-damage tree — it has Retributive Guard, [Tier][Die] SPIRIT (Deflect-ignoring, the strongest damage type in the game per the primer), at depth 1 / level 2. What White lacks is not damage but a damage play it initiates: Retributive Guard is a Reaction that requires an adjacent ally to be hit first, and it competes for the one Reaction slot with six other talents, three of which fire on the identical trigger. Adding a second White damage talent would not change the felt experience at all; re-typing Interposing Shield off that slot (proposal 4) changes it immediately, for free. Blue genuinely is zero, on both independent measures.

Second, damage is the wrong diagnosis of what the two players are feeling. The census that reframes this review is action density, not damage density: leyline/White has 2 Action-costing talents in 25 (8% of slots) and leyline/Blue has 5 (20%), against every deity tree's 5-8 in 9 (~72%) and heroic/Warrior's 13 in 25. The complaint "I do nothing on my turn" and the complaint "I never damage anything" produce the same sentence at the table and have different fixes. If you add a damage talent, you have added ONE more Action-costing slot to a tree with two, and the player still Draws Mana and stares at two spare Actions on every round they do not cast it. If you fix the agency, the player has a turn even in the rounds they choose not to attack. Proposal 3 gives Blue a repeatable level-2 on-turn play; proposal 4 unclogs White's Reaction slot; neither adds a point of damage.

Third, both intent files are unusually explicit and both trees deliver what they promise. INTENT-leyline-Blue.md: "They rarely meet force with force. A Blue mage prefers to know, to prepare, and to redirect." INTENT-leyline-White.md: "They draw their power from unity rather than self. A White mage rarely wins alone." Blue implements all three of its promised specialties, and is the only tree in all 365 that CREATES illusions. White scores protection 5 and is the reference implementation of that axis. The design guide's boundary rule ("Talents must not bleed across color lines") is the standard these two trees pass most cleanly. Adding damage to either is the only proposal in this whole review that makes the ecosystem measurably LESS differentiated — you would take the two trees with the sharpest non-damage identities and move them toward the middle of a matrix where six trees already do damage well.

Fourth, and this is the practical argument: the same felt outcome is available without damage and the engine already supports it. The primer records that `edha-next-test-mod` carries a `formula` field applied by term concatenation, that item 49 made those entries SUM, and that it is used today by exactly one adversary ability and zero talents. Blue's five disadvantage talents currently fold into one binary scalar — five talents doing one talent's work, which is the single largest waste of slots in the tree. Converting two or three of them (Pattern Recognition, False Premise, Probability Cascade are the natural set) from binary disadvantage to a summing formula penalty makes them additive, makes Blue's numbers go visibly down on the enemy's sheet, uses an existing primitive, and is entirely on-identity for a specialty literally named Calculation. I do not rank it above proposal 3 because the objection is real — uncapped additive penalties are the ecosystem's largest identified balance risk and the primitive is unproven on talents — so if it is done it should be capped (e.g. total penalty never worse than -1[Die], or a maximum of two stacking sources) and benched before it ships. But it is the answer to "Blue needs teeth", and it is not damage.

What would change my mind, concretely: (1) if the agency fixes land and the Blue player still reports feeling like a spectator after two sessions, then the diagnosis was wrong and Blue should get ONE conditional damage channel — my choice would be to retune Absolute Stillness or Ghostly Walls to add damage against a 0-Speed target, so the damage is the payoff of Blue's own lock rather than a new attack, keeping "rarely meets force with force" true; (2) if the adversary pack shows that fights are routinely won or lost on raw HP throughput, so that a party carrying two zero-damage PCs cannot clear encounters at all — that is a question the scope fence excludes and it would be settled by reading the adversary statblocks and the encounter-budget rules, not by any further reading of the 365.

FOR WHITE SPECIFICALLY, MY ANSWER IS FLATLY NO, with no conditions. White's one damage talent is already the correct amount, it is already the game's best damage type, and the tree's protection-5 identity is the one thing in the leyline atlas that nothing else in 21 trees replicates.
argumentOnSovereignty:
Sovereignty needs a documentation retraction and a card-text line, not a rebuild — and the case against rebuilding it is stronger than the review's headline suggests. The tree's real defect is a promise: both intent sources print Decree as "a declared law projected within a radius", the deity guide repeats it with a loop ("diminish target -> elevate ally -> bring them into Decree"), and no Sovereignty talent creates a zone, a radius or an aura; all nine are single-target, and "Decree" survives only inside the talent name "Decree of Ruin". A player meets that gap before they ever roll a die, because the path description is what they read when choosing a god. Retracting it costs nothing and is the whole minimal-change fix (proposal 6a).

The second real defect is invisible rather than absent: every Sovereignty card prints "[Tier][Die]" with no colour, and exactly one talent is sized by White (Sovereign's Favor's temp HP, `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2)`). So a player who has paid the White 3+ gate — a level-6, six-skill-rank investment — cannot tell from any card what it bought. Printing "[Tier][Die on White]" closes it. Note that this also settles the "four of five deity toll booths are White" narrative in the negative: counting both the `@skills.<colour>.rank` formulas and the `color`/`rangeColor` targeting fields in the authored overlays, exactly ONE pure toll booth exists in the entire deity atlas (Fate/White, zero references of either kind), and three of the four near-dead gates are not White. That finding should not drive any change beyond the Fate/White line and the Sovereignty card text.

What I would NOT do under a minimal-change framing is fix the tree's third and deepest problem: nine talents built from two repeated clauses, with a payload (one die step = +1.0 average per die, worth exactly zero against the four flat-damage riders in the corpus) that sits below the threshold at which a person at a table notices anything happened. That is a tree rewrite, not an edit, and the defence of the tree is genuinely strong on structure — Sovereign's Favor's [Tier][Die] temp HP is unmediated by the die ladder and repeatable from L2, Expose is a free L2 Passive generating Investiture uncapped and converting every enemy miss into an ally Reactive Strike, Edict of the Fallen is a scene-long -2 steps plus party temp HP for 2 Actions at L3, and the capstone carries a scene-long enemy reaction lock. The tree's "damage_direct 0, nine axes at zero" headline is substantially a rubric artefact: deity/Knowledge does the identical job (convert a mark into a party-wide damage multiplier) and scores 5/5 because it also holds a sword, while Sovereignty amplifies through an ally and scores 0. Same function, opposite scores. If the designer wants the Decree promise kept rather than retracted, the one-talent version is to give the capstone a radius (proposal 6c) — a capstone is where a radius belongs and it delivers the whole promised gesture without a new mechanic. Otherwise: retract the promise, print the colour, and revisit the tree after playtest-1 with actual table evidence about whether a die step is perceptible.
